diseases.name: Leaf Blight
symptoms: Brown or tan spots on leaves
Wilting and yellowing of leaf edges
cure: Remove and destroy infected leaves immediately
Apply copper-based fungicide (2g per liter water)
Spray Mancozeb 75% WP at 2.5g per liter
Improve air circulation around plants
Avoid overhead watering
organicRemedies: Sour Buttermilk Spray (खट्टी छाछ): Dilute 50ml fermented sour buttermilk (kept 4 days in copper vessel) in 1L water; spray weekly. Natural lactic acid arrests blight fungi.
Cold-Pressed Neem Oil (5ml/L) emulsified with 2ml natural liquid soap; spray every 5-7 days in late evening.
Trichoderma harzianum bio-fungicide (5g/L) root drench to stop soil-borne fungal spore progression.
Organic Soil Boost: Mix 250g Vermicompost + 50g Neem cake powder at base to build natural systemic resistance.
plantCareSuggestions: Sanitary Pruning: Prune infected bottom 6 inches of leaves to break fungal splash cycle.
Irrigate strictly at root level early morning; keep leaves dry.
Apply 2-3 inch dry straw or biomass mulch over soil to prevent spore splash during rains.

diseases.name: Powdery Mildew
cure: Spray neem oil solution (5ml per liter water)
Apply sulfur-based fungicide
Use baking soda spray (1 tbsp per gallon water)
Apply Karathane 0.05% spray
Remove severely infected parts
organicRemedies: Baking Soda & Neem Foliar Spray: Dissolve 5g sodium bicarbonate (मीठा सोडा) + 5ml pure neem oil in 1L water; disrupts fungal spore membranes.
Raw Cow Milk Solution: 1 part milk to 9 parts water; sunlight activates natural antiseptic lactoferrin enzymes.
Wood Ash (लकड़ी की राख): Sift dry wood ash and lightly dust onto damp foliage early morning to create an alkaline barrier hostile to fungal germination.
Panchagavya Foliar Spray (30ml/L) to strengthen leaf cuticles and boost photosynthetic activity.
plantCareSuggestions: Ensure 6-8 hours of direct sunlight daily and avoid shaded, humid pockets.
Prune dense inner foliage to provide continuous air circulation through the plant canopy.
Avoid excess synthetic nitrogen fertilizers which cause soft, succulent leaves vulnerable to mildew.
prevention: Water at the base, not on foliage

diseases.name: Root Rot
symptoms: Yellowing and dropping of lower leaves
diseases.causes: Overwatering and poor drainage (Pythium, Phytophthora fungi)
cure: Stop watering immediately and let soil dry
Remove plant, trim rotten roots with sterile scissors
Apply Trichoderma viride to soil (5g per kg soil)
Repot in fresh, well-draining soil mix
Apply systemic fungicide (Metalaxyl 8% WP)
organicRemedies: Trichoderma viride Bio-Fungicide: Inoculate 10g Trichoderma per plant into moist vermicompost, apply into topsoil around root zone.
Cow Urine & Turmeric Drench: Mix 100ml fresh cow urine + 10g pure turmeric powder in 2L water; drench soil around infected roots.
Wood Charcoal & Sand Mix: Blend powdered charcoal and coarse river sand into root perimeter to absorb stagnant toxins and aerate.
Pseudomonas fluorescens biological soil treatment (10ml/L) to colonize roots and suppress Pythium.
plantCareSuggestions: Immediately withhold watering until top 2-3 inches of soil completely dry out.
Improve bed drainage by adding raised beds or drilling larger container drainage holes.
Gently aerate root zone soil with a hand fork to introduce oxygen to suffocating roots.
prevention: Water only when top inch of soil is dry
Add perlite or sand to heavy soils

diseases.name: Nitrogen Deficiency
symptoms: Pale green to yellow leaves (starting from older leaves)
diseases.causes: Insufficient nitrogen in soil, leaching from heavy rain
cure: Apply urea fertilizer (46-0-0) at 2-3g per plant
Use ammonium sulfate for quick nitrogen boost
Apply vermicompost (200g per plant)
Foliar spray of 2% urea solution
Add composted manure around the base
organicRemedies: Liquid Jeevamrutha (तरल जीवामृत): Apply 10% solution directly to root zone to trigger rapid nitrogen-fixing microbial blooms.
Mustard Cake Liquid Fertilizer (सरसों की खली की चाय): Soak 250g mustard cake in 5L water for 4 days, dilute 1:10 and drench soil.
Vermicompost Top-Dressing: Spread 300g worm-castings enriched with Azotobacter bio-fertilizer per plant.
Compost Tea Foliar Spray: Brew well-aerated compost tea and spray on leaves for fast foliar nitrogen uptake.
plantCareSuggestions: Intercrop with nitrogen-fixing legumes (beans, cowpea, clover) to biologically fix atmospheric nitrogen.
Apply thick organic mulch (dry leaves/compost) to prevent nitrogen leaching during irrigation.

diseases.name: Phosphorus Deficiency
symptoms: Purple or reddish discoloration on leaves
diseases.causes: Low phosphorus in soil, acidic or cold soils
cure: Apply Single Super Phosphate (SSP) at 5g per plant
Use bone meal (1 tablespoon per plant)
Apply DAP (Di-Ammonium Phosphate) at 3g per plant
Add rock phosphate for slow release
Adjust soil pH to 6.0-7.0 range
organicRemedies: Steamed Bone Meal: Apply 2 tablespoons (30g) bone meal into root zone for slow, natural phosphorus release.
Rock Phosphate & PSB (Phosphate Solubilizing Bacteria): Mix 20g rock phosphate + 5g PSB per plant in compost.
Banana Peel & Wood Ash Compost: Fermented banana peel tea provides readily bioavailable natural phosphorus.
plantCareSuggestions: Maintain soil pH in the sweet spot of 6.2 - 6.8 so native phosphorus doesn't get chemically locked up.
Ensure soil warmth and aeration; cold, compacted soil inhibits root phosphorus absorption.

diseases.name: Potassium Deficiency
symptoms: Browning and scorching of leaf margins
Poor fruit quality and small size
diseases.causes: Sandy or light soils, heavy rainfall leaching
cure: Apply Muriate of Potash (MOP) at 3g per plant
Use Sulfate of Potash (SOP) for sensitive crops
Add wood ash around plants (handful per plant)
Banana peel fertilizer (dried and powdered)
Foliar spray of 1% KCl solution
organicRemedies: Wood Ash (लकड़ी की राख): Sprinkle 1 handful of hardwood ash around base (contains 5-7% natural bio-potash).
Fermented Banana Peel Extract: Soak 4-5 banana peels in 2L water for 72 hours; use liquid as high-potash root drench.
KMB (Potash Mobilizing Bacteria): Inoculate soil with KMB bio-fertilizer to solubilize insoluble soil potassium.
plantCareSuggestions: Mulch heavily with dry biomass to minimize potassium leaching.
Water evenly to allow steady nutrient uptake without drying stress.

diseases.name: Aphid Infestation
symptoms: Clusters of small green/black insects on stems
Black sooty mold on leaf surface
diseases.causes: Aphid insects (Aphis spp.), attracted by tender growth
cure: Spray neem oil (5ml per liter water) every 7 days
Release ladybugs (natural predators)
Strong water spray to dislodge aphids
Apply insecticidal soap spray
Spray Imidacloprid 17.8% SL (0.5ml per liter)
organicRemedies: Dashparni Ark (दशपर्णी अर्क) / Herbal Concoction: Spray 20ml per liter water; repels aphids and sucking pests instantly.
Garlic-Chilli-Soap Spray (अग्न्यास्त्र): Boil crushed garlic and pungent hot green chilies with water, add 2 drops soap, spray underside.
5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE): Wash underside of leaves thoroughly where aphids colonize.
Yellow Sticky Traps: Hang yellow sheets coated with castor oil at crop canopy height.
plantCareSuggestions: Companion planting: Plant French Marigold (गेंदा), Sweet Basil, and Coriander around boundaries to repel pests and attract ladybugs.
Blast underside of leaves with a firm water spray to dislodge nymphs mechanically.

diseases.name: Overwatering Stress
symptoms: Yellowing of leaves starting from bottom
Mold or algae on soil surface
cure: Stop watering and let soil dry completely
Move plant to a well-ventilated area
Remove standing water from saucers
If severe, repot in dry soil
Add perlite to improve drainage
organicRemedies: Topsoil Aeration & Dry Wood Ash: Lightly cultivate topsoil and dust with wood ash to absorb excess surface moisture.
Apply Mycorrhizal fungi (VAM) to rejuvenate damaged root hair absorption capacity.
plantCareSuggestions: Never water on a fixed calendar; always check soil 2 inches below surface before watering.
Ensure containers have unblocked drain holes and elevate pots off saucers.
prevention: Use the finger test (dry 1 inch = water)
Ensure drainage holes in all containers

diseases.name: Sunburn / Heat Stress
symptoms: White or bleached patches on leaves
Wilting during hottest part of day
diseases.causes: Excessive direct sunlight, sudden exposure change
cure: Move plant to partial shade immediately
Use shade cloth (30-50% shade)
Water deeply in early morning
Apply mulch to keep roots cool
Remove severely damaged leaves
organicRemedies: Seaweed Extract (2ml/L) foliar spray in the evening to stimulate anti-stress phyto-hormones.
Aloe Vera & Water foliar wash: 50ml fresh aloe gel blended in 1L water creates a soothing protective bio-layer.
plantCareSuggestions: Erect 50% green agro-shade netting over sensitive plants during peak hours (11 AM - 3 PM).
Mulch generously around base with dry hay to keep root rhizosphere cool.

diseases.name: Bacterial Wilt
symptoms: Brown discoloration in stem vascular tissue
Slimy bacterial ooze when stem is cut
diseases.causes: Ralstonia solanacearum bacteria, spread by soil and water
cure: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately
Do NOT compost infected material
Solarize soil for 4-6 weeks before replanting
Apply Streptocycline 500ppm to remaining plants
Drench soil with Bleaching powder (10g per liter)
organicRemedies: Pseudomonas fluorescens Bio-Pesticide (10g/L): Drench root zones of all neighboring plants to build antagonistic biological barrier against Ralstonia.
Turmeric & Fermented Cow Urine Drench: 200ml cow urine + 15g pure raw turmeric powder in 2L water; acts as a powerful natural bactericide.
Neem Cake Soil Application: Work 100g neem cake powder per plant into soil to suppress bacterial populations.
Bio-Solarization: Solarize bed with clear polythene mulch during peak summer for 4-6 weeks to sanitize topsoil naturally.
plantCareSuggestions: Immediately rogue out and safely incinerate wilting plants; do not allow wash water to touch neighboring plants.
Sterilize pruning knives and tools with 70% alcohol or boiling water after every cut.
Practice strict 3-year crop rotation with non-host crops like corn or sorghum.

fertilizers.name: Urea (46-0-0)
fertilizers.caution: Avoid excess – can burn roots. Don't apply on wet foliage.

fertilizers.name: DAP (18-46-0)
fertilizers.caution: Keep away from direct seed contact.

fertilizers.name: MOP (0-0-60)
fertilizers.usage: Improve fruit quality and disease resistance
fertilizers.caution: Avoid in saline soils. Don't mix with urea.

fertilizers.name: NPK Complex (19-19-19)
fertilizers.dosage: 3-5g per liter water (foliar) or 5g per plant

fertilizers.name: Vermicompost (Organic)
fertilizers.dosage: 200-500g per plant or 5 tons per hectare
fertilizers.caution: Ensure it's fully decomposed. No overuse issues.

fertilizers.name: Neem Cake (Organic)
fertilizers.when: Before planting or during soil preparation
fertilizers.caution: Allow 7 days before sowing after application.

fertilizers.name: Bone Meal (Organic)
fertilizers.caution: Slow release – takes weeks to show results.

fertilizers.name: Seaweed Extract
fertilizers.when: During active growth and stress periods
fertilizers.caution: Non-toxic and safe for all crops.

wateringGuide.name: Vegetables
tips: Water at the base, not on leaves
Mulch to retain soil moisture
Increase watering during flowering & fruiting
Reduce in cloudy/rainy weather

wateringGuide.name: Leafy Greens
wateringGuide.frequency: Daily in summer, every 2 days in winter
tips: Keep soil consistently moist but not soggy
Shallow roots need frequent light watering
Use shade nets in extreme heat
Harvest early morning for best freshness

wateringGuide.name: Fruit Trees
tips: Deep water to encourage deep root growth
Reduce watering during dormant season
Increase during flowering and fruit set
Mulch with organic material (4 inches)

wateringGuide.name: Grains & Cereals
wateringGuide.best_time: Morning or as per irrigation schedule
tips: Rice: Maintain 2-5cm standing water during growth
Wheat: 4-6 irrigations at critical stages
Corn: Critical watering at tasseling stage
Avoid water stress during grain filling

wateringGuide.name: Flowers & Ornamentals
wateringGuide.method: Drip or hand watering at base
tips: Avoid wetting flower petals
Roses need deep weekly watering
Marigolds are drought tolerant once established
Group plants by water needs

tips.title: 🌱 Soil Preparation
tips.tip: Test soil pH before planting. Most vegetables prefer pH 6.0-7.0. Add lime for acidic soil, sulfur for alkaline soil.

tips.title: 🌿 Companion Planting
tips.tip: Plant basil near tomatoes to repel pests. Marigolds near vegetables deter aphids and whiteflies naturally.

tips.title: 💧 Watering Wisdom
tips.tip: Water deeply but less frequently to encourage deep root growth. Morning watering is best to reduce disease risk.

tips.title: 🐛 Natural Pest Control
tips.tip: Spray neem oil (5ml/L water) every 7-10 days as a preventive measure. It's safe and effective against most pests.

tips.title: 🌾 Crop Rotation
tips.tip: Rotate crops every season: Root crops → Leafy crops → Fruiting crops → Legumes. This prevents soil depletion.

tips.title: 🧪 Organic Composting
tips.tip: Create compost from kitchen waste: peels, tea leaves, eggshells. Mix with dry leaves. Ready in 45-60 days.

tips.title: ✂️ Pruning Technique
tips.tip: Prune dead/diseased branches at a 45° angle. Sterilize cutting tools with rubbing alcohol between cuts.

tips.title: 🌡️ Temperature Care
tips.tip: Protect seedlings from extreme heat with shade nets (30-50%). In winter, use mulch to insulate roots.

tips.title: 🌻 Sunlight Needs
tips.tip: Most vegetables need 6-8 hours of direct sunlight. Leafy greens can tolerate partial shade (4-6 hours).

tips.title: 🪴 Mulching Benefits
tips.tip: Apply 3-4 inches of organic mulch (straw, leaves). Retains moisture, suppresses weeds, and adds nutrients.

tips.title: 🧬 Seed Selection
tips.tip: Choose disease-resistant varieties for your region. Treat seeds with Trichoderma before sowing for better germination.

tips.title: 📅 Seasonal Planting
tips.tip: Kharif (June-Oct): Rice, Cotton, Soybean. Rabi (Oct-Mar): Wheat, Mustard, Peas. Zaid (Mar-Jun): Watermelon, Cucumber.

tips.title: 🔬 Soil Testing
tips.tip: Test soil every 6 months for NPK, pH, and organic content. Contact your nearest agriculture office for free testing.

tips.title: 💪 Plant Immunity
tips.tip: Spray Pseudomonas fluorescens (10g/L) to boost plant immunity. Apply Trichoderma viride to soil for root protection.

tips.title: 🍃 Micronutrients
tips.tip: Yellowing between leaf veins = Iron/Magnesium deficiency. Spray micronutrient mixture (2g/L) every 15 days.

requests.symptoms: Lower leaves showing brown concentric circular spots with yellow halos. Spreading rapidly after heavy monsoon rain.
requests.adminRemedy:
1. Remove and bury severely infected lower leaves.
2. Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L water.
3. Increase spacing and mulch around plant base to prevent soil splash.

requests.symptoms: Upper leaf tips turning pale yellow, stunted tillering, leaves are thin and upright.
requests.adminRemedy: Recommended top-dressing with Urea @ 25 kg/acre after first irrigation.

requests.symptoms: Curling leaves, sticky honeydew on foliage, clusters of tiny green insects under leaves.
